Real tube-transfer validation uses 20 trials per condition: 3DGS/standard-background normalized progress is 66%/17%, not success rate. The v3 main text states 10 real + 90 simulated demonstrations, but the appendix states 100 real demonstrations; this discrepancy needs clarification. This is not established simulation-only zero-shot transfer. | [AM.MAN.DEX.BENCH.5] <a id="am-man-dex-bench-5"></a> | **DexHoldem｜Agent closed-loop evaluation · Scene preservation · Real-world dexterous manipulation**<br>[DexHoldem: An Agentic Robotics Benchmark for Dexterous Manipulation in Texas Hold'em](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.18727v3)<br>Feng Chen, Tianzhe Chu, Li Sun, Pei Zhou, Zhuxiu Xu, Shenghua Gao, Yuexiang Zhai, Yanchao Yang, Yi Ma<br>**Tags:** `agent-benchmark` `benchmark` `dexterous` `shadowhand` `real-world` `teleoperation-dataset` `instruction-conditioned-policy` `imitation-learning` [vla](../../topics/vla.md) `multi-view` `scene-preservation` `structured-state-perception` `rule-based-routing` `closed-loop-verification` `primitive-retry` `long-horizon-evaluation` | **Hands:** One hand type: a single ShadowHand on UR10e, using a shared 30-D joint-position interface (six arm and 24 hand channels). Left/right labels refer to card positions, not a bimanual setup.<br>**Tasks:** Fourteen primitives: two each for card pickup, placement and revealing, plus push/pull for four chip denominations. There are 1,470 real teleoperated trajectories, with 100 training and five validation examples per primitive, plus 36 state-perception problems scored over eight field categories.<br>**Same-task cross-hand reuse:** The same primitives/interface compare policy models, but physical evaluation is limited to ShadowHand; matched cross-hand evaluation and shared-policy transfer to other hands are not demonstrated.<br>**Release:** Hugging Face releases three-view RGB-D/joint-state data. Official repositories provide policy training/deployment and agent runtime/perception evaluation, with six public policy-training recipes. The paper's simulation component documents real-to-sim reconstruction and open-loop replay, not quantitative policy evaluation; complete simulation-asset and trained task-policy weight availability is unverified.<br>**Key distinction:** DexHoldem combines fourteen real ShadowHand tabletop primitives and 1,470 demonstrations with policy, agent-perception and closed-loop evaluation, separating task completion from scene preservation to expose the gap between isolated skill success and multi-step system reliability.<br>**Evaluation scope:** A dedicated agent camera feeds structured tabletop memory; deterministic routing handles waiting, verification and recovery, querying the agent at decision states and translating high-level choices into low-level primitives. A demonstration-trained/fine-tuned policy maps three-view images, proprioception and primitive conditions to 30-D joint-target chunks; feedback changes state and dispatch, not weights online. Pickup is verified and the held card read before replacement; harmless failures may retry per primitive, while disrupted scenes request human help. Nine policies receive 80 physical trials each (720 total). Pi-0.5 reaches 61.2% task completion; pi-0.5/pi-0 tie at 47.5% scene-preserving success. System evaluation covers only GPT-5.5 + pi-0: four of 33 hands complete, including one with human assistance and three without a help request; only one needs neither retries nor help. Twelve of 34 retry dispatches restore their primitive. Perception problems supply annotated predecessor context, rather than testing autonomous long-term memory; fixed-vocabulary execution does not establish unseen-language generalization. | arXiv v3 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.18727v3) · [Code](https://github.com/DexHoldem/Dexholdem-Policy) · [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Winniechen2002/TexasPokerRobot) · [Assets](https://github.com/DexHoldem/DexHoldemSKills) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-27 |
